content: 1. The use of pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Patients should avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs, except for bedaquiline and linezolid. 2. Prochlorperazine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should be avoided or replaced with alternative medications. 3. Promazine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should be avoided or replaced with alternative medications. 4. Promethazine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should be avoided or replaced with alternative medications. 5. Protriptyline and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should be avoided or replaced with alternative medications. 6. Rabeprazole reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This may elevate creatine kinase levels and increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, as red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase regorafenib levels while reducing exposure to its active metabolites M-2 and M-5. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Ketoconazole and ribociclib mutually increase each other's effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Ribociclib also increases ketoconazole levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Ketoconazole increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with combined P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as this combination may significantly increase rivaroxaban levels and bleeding risk. 15. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients starting ruxolitinib while on strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, adjust the starting dose based on platelet counts. For patients already on ruxolitinib, reduce the dose by 50% when initiating a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients on low-dose ruxolitinib. 17. Ketoconazole decreases the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Systemic or oral antifungals may reduce probiotic activity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage and resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 21. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors when sildenafil is used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. For erectile dysfunction, consider reducing the initial sildenafil dose to 25 mg and monitor for toxicities such as dyspepsia, headache, and hypotension. 22. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of siponimod with drugs that moderately or strongly inhibit both CYP2C9 and CYP3A4. 23. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed a solifenacin dose of 5 mg/day when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Ketoconazole and sparsentan increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 29. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the sunitinib dose based on the indication and avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Ketoconazole increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce tadalafil clearance, leading to increased systemic exposure and significant adverse events such as severe hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of talazoparib through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition, which may increase systemic exposure. If coadministration cannot be avoided, monitor for potential adverse reactions. 35. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the potential for increased toxicity. 36. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Thioridazine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 41. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg/day when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 42. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed a tolterodine dose of 2 mg/day when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 43. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of topotecan by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. 45. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of toremifene by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 47. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both trazodone and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Trifluoperazine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Trimipramine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 52. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%. Reduce the vilazodone daily dose to 20 mg. 54. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 55. Ketoconazole and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 56. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. 61. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of amikacin by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Ketoconazole and apomorphine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the aripiprazole oral dose by 50% when used with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Further reduce to 25% of the usual dose in patients also receiving strong CYP2D6 inhibitors or who are CYP2D6 poor metabolizers. 66. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Arsenic trioxide and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
